comment: Development-agent controls (R12 GOV-9067, SEC-9068, SEC-9077, SEC-9078, SEC-9084, CICD-9076, CICD-9082, CICD-9083), read by scripts/agent-guard.mjs and scripts/agent-lanes.mjs. The role table mirrors '## Paths you may change' in each .claude/agents/*.md; scripts/agent-guard.test.mjs fails when the two disagree, so a role cannot widen in one place only. Editing this file is itself a protected change: an agent-authored commit touching it needs a person's approving review.

agent_markers.comment: How a commit is recognised as agent-authored. Any one marker is enough. Matching is case-insensitive on the whole value. An agent session that pushes as its user, with none of these, is invisible to every check here; that limit is stated in docs/ops/runbooks/development-agent-controls.md rather than hidden.

protected_paths.comment: Paths an agent-authored change may touch only with an approving review from a person who is not an agent. These are the files that decide what every other check means: the workflows, the agents' own instructions and settings, the gates' scripts and policies, the paper-trading boundary's Terraform layer, the owner's switches (every environment's tfvars), the dependency allow-list, and the four guard suites .github/CODEOWNERS names as the non-negotiables' own tests (R12-ARCH-9071): an agent that could rewrite architecture.rs or paper_boundary.rs in the same change as the code they guard could redefine a non-negotiable with one review and no person.

unmarked_protected_change.comment: GOV-9067. A change with no agent marker is a person's only by default, and an agent pushing as its user with no trailer is exactly that default. On a protected path the default is not accepted: every commit must carry a signature GitHub verified against a key a person registered, or a person must approve the head commit. GitHub's own web-flow key signs every commit made through the API or the web editor, an agent's included, so a commit it signed is not a person's signature; its committer address is listed here so the guard can tell.

dispatch_refused_for_agents.comment: Workflows an agent identity may never start: each deploys, applies infrastructure or reaches a cloud credential. A planner may read and plan; no agent merges or deploys (GOV-9067). Enforced by the guard step at the top of each workflow, before anything authenticates.

deploy_range_advisory.comment: ADR 0124 §3 (the owner accepted this on 2026-10-12 citing ADR 0123, whose record was never written; 0123 is the ledger-operations ADR, and 0124 records this decision under its own number). dev reads the agent-boundary range verdict as advice: refusals are printed, the deploy proceeds. The guard admits only dev whatever this list says.

self_reviewable_protected_paths.comment: ADR 0124 §1, owner-accepted 2026-10-18. Protected paths an agent-authored change may touch without a person's approval of the head commit: the ADR index when GitHub reports it modified (globs), and a NEW decision record when GitHub reports it added (added_only_globs). Both are judged by the status GitHub returns for the file: a bare path, a removed, renamed or copied file, and an edit to an accepted ADR all still need a person, and a rename is judged on the path it left as well as the one it took. Nothing under .claude/rules/ is here — the domain notes carry Prohibited lists that bind agents, and the session's own permission layer refused an agent edit to its rules as self-modification. Everything else protected keeps the rule above: every rule file, CLAUDE.md, every workflow, every gate script and policy (this file included), the tfvars and the paper-trading Terraform layer. A change touching one self-reviewable path and one other protected path still needs the approval, and the refusal names only the paths that need it.

lane_manifest.comment: The current round's lane plan, a path relative to the repository root. An agent commit carrying `Agent-Lane: <id>` is held to that lane's `owns` by agent-guard.mjs, on the pull request and at deploy; a trailer naming no lane in this file is refused. Point it at the next round's manifest in the same protected change that commits it. `trailer_required_after` (CICD-9083): when set to an ISO 8601 instant, every agent commit committed at or after it must carry an Agent-Lane trailer naming a lane in the manifest above; earlier commits are not judged. Unset (null) on purpose when this was written: round-3.json names no lane of the round now running, so turning it on before that round's manifest is committed would refuse every lane's commits. Set it in the same protected change that points `path` at the running round's manifest.

lane_limits.comment: Every lane an orchestrator dispatches carries a budget no larger than these, and acceptance commands. The sandbox workflow sets its job timeout from the lane's own minutes. `tokens` and `usd` are what the lane may spend on models; `agent-lanes.mjs spend` refuses a lane whose model-gateway ledger shows more, and a ledger line whose spend it cannot read counts as over (SEC-9077).

sandbox.comment: The agent sandbox's network (SEC-9077, SEC-9078; ADR 0117). agent-sandbox.yml runs a lane's acceptance under a group the runner's firewall lets reach loopback only, DNS included, so scripts/agent-egress.mjs is the one way out: HTTPS CONNECT to these hosts on 443, within these quotas, and nothing else. No model provider is listed, so a lane cannot call a model from the sandbox at all; scripts/agent-egress.test.mjs fails if one is added. Every host here is a package registry, and each accepts uploads with a credential the sandbox does not hold; that residual is named in ADR 0117.
